channel.title: Brain Blog – try4ever.com
channel.description: Notes on studying, memory and building Brain – a 3D knowledge map tool for students.

item.title: Finals Week: From Cramming to Calm
item.description: All-nighters feel heroic and perform terribly. Finals week, rebuilt in four evenings: map it, quiz it, space it, sleep.

item.title: Parents: See Your Child's Real Progress
item.description: 'I already studied, mom.' Meta-analyses link family involvement to real achievement gains – if you can see the studying. Now you can.

item.title: Teachers: Cut the Busywork, Keep the Craft
item.description: Teachers work about 53 hours a week. AI should sharpen your craft, never replace it – here's a tool that takes the busywork, not the teaching.

item.title: FE Exam: Engineering Formulas, Mapped
item.description: The FE exam spans a dozen disciplines in one day. Thermodynamics, statics, ethics, econ – mapped, they finally behave like one subject.

item.title: Language Exams: Map Your Way to Fluency
item.description: IELTS, TOEFL, JLPT, DELE – language exams test grammar in motion. Grammar patterns, vocab families and keigo all map beautifully.

item.title: GCSE & A-Levels: Revision You Can See
item.description: Revision guides pile up, exam boards differ, and 'just revise' helps nobody. GCSE and A-Level students: make the revision visible.

item.title: AP, SAT, ACT: Big Exams, Small Panic
item.description: AP exams, the SAT and the ACT reward students who can see structure. High schoolers: here's how to study smarter, not just longer.

item.title: CPA & CFA: Mountains of Material, Mapped
item.description: Accounting and finance exams bury you in standards and formulas. Maps turn FAR, AUD, REG and the CFA curriculum into visible structure.

item.title: Law Exams: See the Whole Case Map
item.description: Law school hides its structure inside hundreds of pages. IRAC, elements and exceptions become navigable when you can see the case map.

item.title: NCLEX Pharmacology That Finally Sticks
item.description: 317,710 candidates sat the NCLEX last year – and a 73% pass rate means most walk in under-prepared. Pharmacology is where maps win.

item.title: MCAT Prep: Stop Rereading, Start Retrieving
item.description: More than 23,000 students matriculate into U.S. med schools each year – most of them beat the MCAT with retrieval, not rereading.

item.title: USMLE Step 1 Without the All-Nighter
item.description: About 25,000 U.S. and Canadian students take Step 1 every year. The exam tests connections, not lists – study it that way.

item.title: Spaced Repetition vs 3D Maps: Use Both
item.description: Flashcard schedules and 3D maps solve different problems. The strongest study systems refuse to choose – here's how to combine them.

item.title: Watch Your Mastery Turn From Red to Green
item.description: A progress bar you can see in 3D changes which topics you study next – and it changes how it feels to walk into an exam.

item.title: Why I Built Brain: Notes Into 3D Maps
item.description: Outlines hide the shape of what you're learning. I wanted to see it – so I built a tool that turns your own files into a 3D map.

item.title: The Chat That Changed How I Study
item.description: Two friends. One drowning in notes, one calm before finals. One question in a coffee shop that reveals the entire difference.

item.title: 5 Study Hacks That Actually Survived Testing
item.description: Forget highlighters. Five unconventional study hacks that survived contact with real evidence – including one that involves walking in circles.

item.title: What a Learning Coach Told Me About Systems
item.description: A seasoned learning coach on why motivation is overrated, why systems win, and the three questions to ask before any study session.

item.title: Reading Five Times Is the Worst Way to Study
item.description: Rereading feels productive and delivers almost nothing. The 61%-vs-40% study every student should know – and the 20-minute fix.

item.title: Drowning in Lecture Notes? Here's the Fix
item.description: I used to hate studying. Then I learned to see my whole syllabus at once – and the stack of PDFs turned into a map I could walk.

item.title: Rote Memorization Fails. Your Brain Wants This
item.description: Repeating facts until they hurt is the hardest way to learn. What research says works instead – and how to switch tonight.

item.title: A Poem for Every Tired Student
item.description: Your hippocampus is a constellation of memories. A short poem for the nights when studying feels like falling – and a way back up.

item.title: Why a Map Beats a List for Memory
item.description: Your brain is a navigator, not a filing cabinet. Spatial memory turns lists you forget into places you know – here's the science and the shortcut.
